newsitem.title: ITALY: Kidnapped Italian photographer freed in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Kidnapped Italian photographer freed in Chechnya.

text.p: An Italian magazine photographer who was kidnapped in the Chechen capital Grozny in February has been released in good health and is on his way home, the Italian foreign ministry said on Sunday.
The ministry said in a statement that Mauro Galligani, 55, who worked for the news weekly Panorama, was freed on Saturday night by his captors and arrived in Moscow on Sunday.
"Galligani is in good physical condition although very exhausted by the length of his kidnapping," the statement said.

"He arrived at our embassy in Moscow on a special flight organised by the Italian Foreign Ministry, accompanied by an embassy official, and later continued his journey to Milan where he is expected to arrive later in the evening."

Galligani was kidnapped on February 23 by four armed men who stopped him, a correspondent for the Italian daily Il Giorno, a driver and an interpreter in the city centre and forced the photographer to leave with them.

The ministry statement said Galligani's release was achieved with the help of the Russian and Chechen authorities as well as influential Chechens contacted through the embassy and the humanitarian agency Intersos.
Chechen rebels have successfully resisted the Russian army's efforts since December 1994 to subdue the northern Caucasus region's independence drive.

Russia and the separatists struck a peace deal in August 1996 under which Moscow withdrew its forces from the region while the rebels promised to put off until 2001 any decision on the thorny issue of Chechnya's future political status.
